matches.quote: A 6L flake on Al2O3 would allow a matched comparison with 6L/Au
so a strain- or disorder-induced Tc gradient near Au would give the same signature with no screening at all.
neither direction nor density of transferred charge is estimated. The authors should estimate it ... and compare with doping levels known to shift Tc
The 20–80 cm⁻¹ window of Eq. 1 (Fig. 4K–O) includes the leaked Ag(o1)* mode near 30–35 cm⁻¹ and, below Tc, Ag(m1); Eq. 1 has no background term
They should add spatial Raman maps (or several spots) across the 4L/Au flake to show whether Tc^avg and the broadening are uniform
fit the χ''ac(ω,T) maps and the Ag(m5) onset with a weighted superposition of layers with distinct local Tc; and show that the proposed gradient reproduces the onset, width
Whether it comes from thickness, ALD-induced strain, interface chemistry or heating matters for the baseline used to isolate the Au effect.

Otherwise the abstract and conclusions, including "This suppression affirms the nature of the quasi-elastic peak as being related to critical excitonic fluctuations", should be softened to "consistent with".
fit the χ''ac(ω,T) maps and the Ag(m5) onset with a weighted superposition of layers with distinct local Tc

notes: C4: P6 and P21 criticize the reliability of the 10 cm-1 quasi-elastic metric (due to the 15 cm-1 Rayleigh leak/cutoff and the arbitrary 15% peak threshold), but do not specifically ask how sensitive Tc is to varying the wavenumber, so C4 is judged not raised. C8: P2 quotes the exact sentence on p. 14 where the text reverses which layers are orthorhombic vs monoclinic relative to Fig. 5B inset, but misses the reversal itself. C9: P10 asks to fit the total Raman signal as a weighted superposition of layers rather than subtracting bulk to isolate the interface layer response, so it is scored as partly. C11: P7 questions whether ALD Al2O3 is an unperturbed baseline (citing interface chemistry and ALD strain), partly overlapping with C11's concern about ALD Al2O3 quality.
